cells.tense: You are leading with intent, and the leading is moving things now.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are steering right now, and one thing you are letting someone else steer. Write both down before the day gets loud.
cells.core:
The call is coming from one place, and it is visible to whoever is in the room. How the yes gets said, how the no gets held, how a thing gets taken from started to done — the direction is being set and it lands. That clarity is what makes it work. Nobody has to guess where you stand.

What keeps it healthy is the other thing sitting right next to it: staying open to what you do not know yet. You can move and still be curious about what the moment is showing you. When there is a pause in the charge long enough to hear something new, the direction gets sharper rather than slower. Nothing here asks you to be less decisive. It asks you to keep the aiming on the moment in front of you.
cells.sheetLine: You set the direction and people can see you set it.
cells.place: in the drive toward a goal

cells.tense: You will be bracing against a moment that has not happened yet.
cells.ask: Pick the one goal you are pushing hardest on. For one day, do nothing on it that isn't asked for. Notice what you are afraid will fall apart.
cells.core:
The push has gotten ahead of the thing it is pushing. Somewhere ahead is a version of this that finally works, and the energy is already over there — so what is in front of you gets treated as a problem to solve, and the solving has started to be the point. The charge that used to move things is now mostly moving you.

The information is in the trying. When you notice yourself forcing a shape onto something that has not happened yet, that noticing is not a flaw. The push is not wrong and it does not need to be shut off. It needs a target that exists today, and the one you are pressing on may not be it.
cells.sheetLine: You are ahead of the moment instead of in it.
cells.place: in the drive toward a goal

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that is now behind you, and you have not turned.
cells.ask: Choose one small structure in your week that no longer fits. Change it — a time, a route, a standing plan — and let the change be visible for seven days.
cells.core:
The charge is not landing. The goal is still visible, the direction still known, but the motion is not happening here — and it can look like patience or waiting for the right conditions. Whatever the standing-still was for, this is where things are right now: at the door, facing something that is already behind.

What brings the drive back is not more effort pushed into the quiet. It is a change in structure. Pick one piece of the week that clearly does not fit and change it, slowly, once, so it can be seen. The charge returns through action that has a shape to it. That shape is the move, not the feeling you are waiting for.
cells.sheetLine: The charge stopped landing, and you are facing a closed door.
cells.place: in the drive toward a goal

cells.tense: You are steering this already, and you are talking about it as if it were the weather.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you designed or started, and say out loud, to one person, that you made the call. Just that sentence. Nothing before it and nothing after it.
cells.core:
The direction is being set more often than it is being claimed. The plan changes, the room shifts, and the account of it comes out as things happening or the situation demanding — not as a choice someone made. That is not modesty. It is a habit of not seeing the hand on the wheel.

There is a release inside it that rarely gets named. For something to keep moving, something gets left behind, and the leaving keeps happening quietly. Naming one decision — not defending it, just saying it was yours — puts the hand back on a wheel it is already holding.
cells.sheetLine: You made the call. You are calling it the situation.
cells.place: in the drive toward a goal
